transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Time: 16:00 UTC (scheduled 45 mins, ran 53)
Duration: 53 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jia Chen (OceanCliff, Head of Infrastructure), Marcus Lowe (Security), Priya Rao (Cloud Architect), Leo Martins (ML Platform)

Summary: brief intake call to understand OceanCliff's constraints for private/VPC deployment of Redwood inference. Primary topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress requirements, region gating/data residency, KMS/encryption, timeline for pilot.

Topics:
- Current infra: AWS-first, multi-account, Transit Gateway in use
- Networking: CIDR overlap concerns, peering vs TGW vs PrivateLink, IP planning
- Security/compliance: KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2, SSO/SAML
- Performance: latency targets for in-app prompts (~150ms p50), burst patterns
- Ops: who will manage routing and handoff, runbooks, monitoring hooks

Action items (auto-section): See metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jia: Hi, this is Jia, I lead infra at OceanCliff.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus here, security.
[00:13] Priya: Priya on cloud infra.
[00:15] Leo: Leo, ML infra.
[00:17] Ethan: Ethan here. Good to meet you all.
[00:19] Samira: Great. The objective today is to understand how you want to run Redwood — hosted, dedicated, or private — and specifically the network and compliance constraints for private/VPC deployment. We'll capture any blockers and propose next steps.
[00:33] Jia: To be clear up front, we're leaning private because of PII and regional regulations for EU, but we want to see what the actual network options look like. We run most production workloads in AWS across prox accounts and have a transit gateway.
[00:45] Samira: Got it. Can you describe your current VPC topology and where the inference endpoints would fit?
[00:51] Priya: Sure. We have a central networking account with TGW that attaches to 6 spoke accounts. Most of our services live in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. The ML workloads are in a dedicated ML account. The ML account is peered to our service VPCs via TGW, and we use egress through NAT gateways in each region. We're trying to avoid public egress for inference traffic.
[01:14] Ethan: Makes sense. For Redwood Private we offer two common patterns: 1) Private endpoints — we can provision interface endpoints (PrivateLink-style) into your VPCs; 2) VPC peering or TGW attachments where our inference nodes are in a customer-managed VPC or a peered account. Each has tradeoffs on routing, cross-account limits, and costs.
[01:37] Marcus: Quick question — for PrivateLink, does traffic traverse the public internet at any point? We need to ensure no egress to internet and encrypted in transit.
[01:45] Ethan: No, PrivateLink uses AWS backbone and stays within the region's network. We ensure mTLS between the client and the service and you can require mutual certs. For transit through TGW, traffic also stays within AWS backbone, but the routing and control plane are different.
[02:01] Jia: We're concerned about IP exhaustion and CIDR overlap because our accounts have a bunch of legacy ranges. If your side needs /24 ranges for ENIs that could conflict.
[02:10] Ethan: Understood. For ENI-based PrivateLink endpoints, yes you'll see ENIs in your VPC; those consume IP addresses. For a peering model, we typically ask for a /22 or /21 to avoid fragmentation, but there's some flexibility. We can publish a recommended IP plan.
[02:27] Priya: Also, our security team insists on KMS integration — keys must be customer-managed, and logs must ship to our Splunk instance; we need audit trails for every request.
[02:37] Samira: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can route audit logs to your logging endpoints. We'll attach SOC2 report and our audit logging spec — Ethan will follow up.
[02:45] Marcus: Do you support bringing your own HSM or a CloudHSM-backed KMS?
[02:49] Ethan: We integrate with AWS KMS keys, and you can control key policies. BYOHSM is possible via CloudHSM + KMS but would be part of an enterprise onboarding. We can scope that in the SOW.
[02:59] Jia: Performance: we're targeting interactive latency for a generative assistant embedded in our UI — p50 around 120–180ms, p95 under 400ms for short prompts. Can Redwood hit that from us-west-2?
[03:12] Ethan: It depends on model and token length. For smaller Llama-family-ish models served with optimized kernels we frequently see p50s under 100ms for short prompts in-region. For larger models or longer sequences it's higher. We'll run a bench from a representative client in us-west-2 to validate.
[03:28] Leo: What about bursting? We'll have daily peaks and occasional large batch jobs. We can't have a queue that causes UI latency.
[03:35] Samira: We offer dedicated pools and autoscaling policies; you can reserve capacity for steady-state and enable burst capacity. For private deployments, autoscaling can be tuned and we can define fallback to a slightly cheaper variant if capacity is exhausted — but for initial pilots most customers start with reserved headroom.
[03:51] Marcus: One more on region constraints: we process EU personal data and require that inference never leaves eu-west-1. Does Redwood support model serving pinned to a region with regional-only endpoints?
[04:01] Ethan: Yes. For Private we can ensure service placement in eu-west-1 only, and the endpoints are regional. We'll also allow routing policies to fail closed to non-regional requests.
[04:11] Priya: Great. On networking, we prefer TGW attachments over peering because peering creates N peering connections across many accounts; TGW is simpler for us. Can Redwood attach to our TGW?
[04:22] Ethan: We can. There are two approaches: 1) Redwood hosts a customer-dedicated account with VPCs attached to your TGW (you peer/attach on your side), or 2) we use PrivateLink + interface endpoints in your account which avoids TGW changes. TGW attachment requires coordination on routing tables and propagation, and we'd ask for a contact at NOC — will be in the action items.
[04:45] Jia: There's also the cross-account security boundary. Who manages the VPC that runs your inference nodes in the TGW model?
[04:51] Samira: Typically, Redwood manages the service VPC (we operate it) but it remains logically segregated under a customer-dedicated account. For Private deployments we offer a ‘customer-owned VPC' model as well where you create the VPC and we install our agents. That last model is more work for you but gives more control.
[05:09] Marcus: From a compliance perspective, the customer-owned VPC model is preferable because we control routing and NACLs. However we need to validate the install process and hardening checklists.
[05:18] Ethan: We have a hardened install doc for the customer-managed VPC model; it outlines IAM roles, least privilege, egress rules, and host hardening. We'll send that over.
[05:26] Priya: About egress — we use strict egress control; anything leaving eu-west-1 triggers alerts. If Redwood needs to fetch model weights or updates, can that be done via an approved pipeline?
[05:36] Ethan: Yes, for private we can stage model artifacts in your S3 or via a signed transfer mechanism. We can also provide a pull-based update mechanism that you control.
[05:43] Jia: For pilot scope: we want a single-region private deployment (us-west-2) tied to our ML account, supporting a small team to validate latencies and integration. If that goes well we'll expand to eu-west-1 with data residency constraints. Timeline target is pilot in Q2 2027.
[05:58] Samira: Q2 pilot is doable — we'll propose a pilot SOW. What's your expected traffic during the pilot, and what success metrics will you use?
[06:06] Leo: We'll be doing low-volume interactive testing — maybe 5–10 qps sustained with spikes to 50 qps for short bursts. Success metrics: p50 < 200ms for short prompts, stable throughput at 50 qps without error, and no data egress outside region.
[06:19] Ethan: Good. We'll use that to size the initial reserved capacity. One operational question: how do you want tracing and metrics? We can emit Prometheus metrics and OTLP traces to your collector.
[06:29] Priya: OTLP to our collector is preferred. Also, we want token-level cost visibility if possible.
[06:34] Samira: Our console provides token-level breakdowns per-route and per-model; we can enable those dashboards for your team and also export granular billing. We'll include a sample dashboard link in the follow-up.
[06:45] Marcus: Identity — we use SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SAML for admin access and RBAC integration?
[06:52] Ethan: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for the console. For service-to-service auth in private deployments we recommend mTLS and short-lived certs; we support vault/KMS-based cert rotations.
[07:04] Jia: Any hard limits we should know? For example, ENI quotas or TGW attachments per account?
[07:09] Ethan: ENI quotas are AWS limits — we'll coordinate with your quota owners. TGW attachments also have account limits; if you expect many attachments we can advise on a consolidated approach.
[07:20] Priya: Network ACLs and security groups — we'll need to see the exact ports used.
[07:24] Ethan: We'll publish a minimal port list — typically HTTPS over 443 plus a management port for install. If you're using PrivateLink you'll see interface endpoints; for peering it's standard IP routing.
[07:36] Samira: Quick pause — any major red flags so far from your side?
[07:40] Marcus: From security, not yet, but we want to see the SOC2 and our legal wants to review the data processing addendum.
[07:47] Samira: We'll attach SOC2 and the DPA.
[07:50] Jia: From operations, my concern is CIDR overlap and how much work to re-IP. Could you support NATing or SNAT if overlap exists?
[07:58] Ethan: We can recommend NAT approaches, but SNAT has implications for source IP visibility. For the pilot we can work around via a NAT gateway in your VPC or ask for a unique /22. We'll include options.
[08:11] Leo: For ML infra, are there any special kernel or runtime requirements? Our clusters are GPU-backed for training, but inference will be on CPU/GPU depending on model.
[08:19] Ethan: Redwood Private supports both CPU and GPU nodes. For GPU we support common drivers and tuned kernels; we'll share the supported AMI list and kernel versions.
[08:29] Priya: Are you using any specific CNI that interacts with TGW? We use AWS VPC CNI and rely on ENI IPs.
[08:36] Ethan: We don't require a specific CNI on your side — our footprint is limited to the VPC and ENIs. If you run additional CNIs on your compute nodes, that won't affect the interface endpoints.
[08:46] Samira: Ok let's capture next steps — Ethan, you'll run a quick bench and produce recommendation for us-west-2 sizing; Samira will send SOC2, DPA, and an architecture diagram; Priya will share CIDR blocks and NOC contact. We'll schedule a TGW/peering technical session next week.
[09:03] Jia: Sounds good. Also can you send an example install runbook for the customer-owned VPC model?
[09:09] Ethan: Yes, I'll attach the install runbook and the hardened checklist.
[09:12] Marcus: On the contract/legal side — we may need subprocessor lists and more details on data residency commitments.
[09:18] Samira: Understood — we'll include the subprocessor list in the follow-up and flag the DPA for legal review.
[09:24] Priya: One last question: if we start private but later want to move to dedicated or hosted for cost reasons, is migration supported?
[09:31] Ethan: Yes, we try to keep the API consistent across modes. Migration involves moving model artifacts and updating endpoints but the application layer sees the same API. We can plan a migration path in the SOW.
[09:42] Leo: Great.
[09:43] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and propose times for the deep dive. Anything else?
[09:51] Jia: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:53] Samira: Meeting adjourned.

Notes on quality: Transcription has a mix of named speakers and sometimes generic tags; a few product names were auto-corrected (Red wood -> Redwood, PrivateLink noted as 'private link' a few times). Natural speech fillers and interruptions present.

Recap / Final next steps (short):
- Redwood to send SOC2, DPA, architecture diagram, install runbook, port list, and subprocessor list (Samira/Ethan).
- Redwood SE to run latency bench in us-west-2 and provide sizing/cost estimate (Ethan, due 2027-02-10).
- OceanCliff to provide CIDR blocks and NOC contact (Priya, due 2027-02-06).
- Schedule TGW/peering technical deep dive (target week of 2027-02-08).

End of transcript.
